paper.title: High-Dimensional Dynamic Pricing Under Nonstationarity: Learning and Earning with Change-Point Detection

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional dynamic pricing under non-stationarity (piecewise-stationary sparse GLM demand)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: action is a price p_t in a bounded interval [p_l,p_u]; demand y_t follows a GLM in x_t=(z_t,p_t) with known link; reward is revenue p_t * E[y_t]
Covariates i.i.d. within each stationary segment, distribution may change across segments; bounded entries and (2+delta)-moment condition with min eigenvalue bounded below
Number of change-points Upsilon_T (S_T) and change locations unknown; minimal change size not known
settings.definition_quote: we assume that there exist $\Upsilon_T$ unknown time periods $1\leq\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots <\tau_{\Upsilon_T} <T$ such that $\theta_t \neq \theta_{t + 1}$ if and only if $t \in \{\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_{\Upsilon_T}\}$. ... the demand $y_t$ follows the probability distribution $f(y_t=y|p_t,z_t)= \exp\{(y x_t^{\top}\theta_t-\psi(x_t^{\top}\theta_t))/a(\phi)+h(y)\}$

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional dynamic pricing under non-stationarity (lower bound)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing with GLM demand in (z_t, p_t); revenue reward
Instances must satisfy the SNR spacing condition (Assumption 3) with Upsilon_T change-points
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{P}_T$ be the collection of distributions satisfying Assumptions 1, 2 and 3, with the corresponding $\bm\theta_T$ possessing~$\Upsilon_T$ number of change-points

conditions: Assumptions 1 and 2 (bounded covariates, ||theta_t||_1 <= C_theta, |S(theta_t)|<=s, psi''>0, unique optimal price in [p_l,p_u], covariate moment conditions)
Assumption 3 (SNR/spacing): min((tau_k - tau_{k-1})/l_{k-1}, (tau_{k+1}-tau_k)/l_{k-1}) kappa_k^2 > c_snr^* for all k
tuning: c_lambda, c_gamma, c_m sufficiently large absolute constants

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be the CPDP algorithm with $m=c_ms\log(Td)$, $\lambda=c_{\lambda}\sqrt{\log(Td)}$, and $\gamma=c_{\gamma}s\lambda^2$, where $c_{\lambda}, c_{\gamma}, c_m > 0$ are absolute constants. Under Assumptions~1 and 2, it holds that $R_T^\pi(\bm \theta_T)\leq C \sqrt{\Upsilon_TT}\left(\kappa_{\min}^{-2}\vee {s\log (Td)}\right)$, for any $\bm\theta_T$ that satisfies Assumption 3, where $C > 0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Upsilon_T (number of change-points) mapped to S_T. Regret is expected revenue loss vs clairvoyant optimal price per round (defined through expected revenue r(p,theta,z)), recorded as pseudo_regret. Mapping of pricing problem to continuum_other is approximate.

conditions: All conditions of Theorem 1, including Assumption 3 (SNR/spacing)
Assumption 4: pseudo-true mixture parameter lies in the interior of Theta and within C_M ||theta_{tau_k}-theta_{tau_{k+1}}||_1 of both pre- and post-change parameters

source.label: cor_regret
source.quote: In addition to all the conditions in Theorem 1, suppose that Assumption 4 also holds, we have that $R_T^\pi(\bm \theta_T)\leq C s\sqrt{\Upsilon_T T}\log (Td)$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Bound independent of change size kappa_min; still requires the SNR assumption which involves kappa_k.

conditions: Instances satisfy Assumptions 1, 2 and 3 with exactly Upsilon_T change-points
Hard instances: linear Gaussian demand y_t = alpha_t + beta_t p_t + N(0,1) noise, no covariates, segment lengths proportional to T/((k+1) sum_j 1/(j+1))

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{P}_T$ be the collection of distributions satisfying Assumptions 1, 2 and 3, with the corresponding $\bm\theta_T$ possessing~$\Upsilon_T$ number of change-points, we have that $\inf_{\pi \in \Pi} \sup_{P(\bm\theta_T) \in \mathcal{P}_T} R_T^{\pi}(\bm\theta_T) \geq C\sqrt{T\Upsilon_T}/\log(\Upsilon_T)$, where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.

results.notes: Paper remarks the bound becomes C sqrt(T Upsilon_T) without the SNR assumption (not formally stated as a theorem). Proof via Le Cam / two-point testing on each segment.
